candidates.title: Investigating the Limitations of Transformers with Simple Arithmetic Tasks
candidates.summary: It is found that how a number is represented in its surface form has a strong influence on the model's accuracy, and this result bolsters evidence that subword tokenizers and positional encodings are components in current transformer designs that might need improvement.

candidates.title: Exploring the Numerical Reasoning Capabilities of Language Models: A Comprehensive Analysis on Tabular Data
candidates.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
candidates.summary: A hierarchical taxonomy for numerical reasoning skills with more than ten reasoning types across four levels: representation, number sense, manipulation, and complex reasoning is proposed.

candidates.title: Number Cookbook: Number Understanding of Language Models and How to Improve It
candidates.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
candidates.summary: This work introduces a benchmark covering four common numerical representations and 17 distinct numerical tasks in four major categories, and finetune practical-scale LLMs on proposed NUPA tasks and finds that naive finetuning can improve NUPA a lot on many but not all tasks, and surprisingly, techniques designed to enhance NUPA prove ineffective for finetuning pretrained models.

candidates.title: Do Language Models Understand Measurements?
candidates.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
candidates.summary: This study shows that PLMs lack the capability required for reasoning over measurements, and proposes a simple embedding strategy to better distinguish between numbers and units, which leads to a significant improvement in the probing tasks.

candidates.title: Investigating the Limitations of the Transformers with Simple Arithmetic Tasks
candidates.venue: arXiv.org
candidates.summary: It is concluded that modern pretrained language models can easily learn arithmetic from very few examples, as long as they use the proper surface representation, which bolsters evidence that subword tokenizers and positional encodings are components in current transformer designs that might need improvement.

candidates.title: Dissociating language and thought in large language models
candidates.venue: Trends in Cognitive Sciences

candidates.title: A Survey of Deep Learning for Mathematical Reasoning
candidates.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
candidates.summary: This survey paper reviews the key tasks, datasets, and methods at the intersection of mathematical reasoning and deep learning over the past decade, and evaluates existing benchmarks and methods and discusses future research directions in this domain.

candidates.title: Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision
candidates.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
candidates.summary: This work synthesizes best practices for representing numbers in text and articulate a vision for holistic numeracy in NLP, comprised of design trade-offs and a unified evaluation.

candidates.title: TIMEDIAL: Temporal Commonsense Reasoning in Dialog
candidates.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
candidates.summary: This paper presents the first study to investigate pre-trained LMs for their temporal reasoning capabilities in dialogs by introducing a new task and a crowd-sourced English challenge set, TimeDial, and reveals that the models fail to reason about dialog context correctly; instead, they rely on shallow cues based on existing temporal patterns in context.

candidates.title: Commonsense Knowledge Reasoning and Generation with Pre-trained Language Models: A Survey
candidates.venue: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
candidates.summary: A survey of commonsense knowledge acquisition and reasoning tasks, the strengths and weaknesses of state-of-the-art pre-trained models for commonsense reasoning and generation as revealed by these tasks, and reflects on future research directions are presented.

candidates.title: Investigating Numeracy Learning Ability of a Text-to-Text Transfer Model
candidates.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
candidates.summary: This work investigates the ability of text-to-text transfer learning model (T5), which has outperformed its predecessors in the conventional NLP tasks, to learn numeracy, to struggle considerably in the extrapolation setting across all four tasks.

candidates.title: Identify, Align, and Integrate: Matching Knowledge Graphs to Commonsense Reasoning Tasks
candidates.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
candidates.summary: This work presents an approach to assess how well a candidate KG can correctly identify and accurately fill in gaps of reasoning for a task, which is called KG-to-task match and demonstrates that ATOMIC, an event-inference focused KG, is the best match for SIQA and MCScript2.0, and that the taxonomic ConceptNet and WikiHow-based KGs are the bestmatch for PIQA across all 3 analysis phases.

candidates.title: Beyond Output Matching: Bidirectional Alignment for Enhanced In-Context Learning
candidates.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
candidates.summary: Bidirectional Alignment is proposed to fully leverage the models' preferences for ICL examples to improve the ICL abilities of student models and can consistently outperform existing baselines on a variety of tasks involving language understanding, reasoning, and coding.

candidates.title: Injecting the score of the first-stage retriever as text improves BERT-based re-rankers
candidates.venue: Discover Computing
candidates.summary: A novel approach for combining first-stage lexical retrieval models and Transformer-based re-rankers is proposed, which injects the relevance score of the lexical model as a token into the input of the cross-encoder re-ranker.

candidates.title: On the data requirements of probing
candidates.venue: Findings
candidates.summary: A novel method to estimate the required number of data samples in such experiments is presented and, across several case studies, it is verified that the estimations have sufficient statistical power.

candidates.title: Predicting Numerals in Natural Language Text Using a Language Model Considering the Quantitative Aspects of Numerals
candidates.venue: Workshop on Knowledge Extraction and Integration for Deep Learning Architectures; Deep Learning Inside Out
candidates.summary: This paper measures the NCS acquired by existing neural language models using a masked numeral prediction task as an evaluation task and proposes methods to reflect not only the symbolic aspect but also the quantitative aspect of numerals in the training of language models, using a loss function that depends on the magnitudes of the numerals and a regression model for the masked numal prediction task.

candidates.title: A survey on mathematical reasoning and optimization with large language models
candidates.venue: Intelligent Systems with Applications

candidates.title: AI Safety in Generative AI Large Language Models: A Survey
candidates.venue: arXiv.org
candidates.summary: The background and motivation for the identified harms and risks in the context of LLMs being generative language models are explored, and a comprehensive analysis is created that provides insights for addressing AI safety in LLMs and encourages the development of aligned and secure models.

candidates.title: tasksource: A Large Collection of NLP tasks with a Structured Dataset Preprocessing Framework
candidates.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
candidates.summary: This work fine-tune a multi-task text encoder on all tasksource tasks, outperforming every publicly available text encoder of comparable parameter count according to an external evaluation.

candidates.title: LangBridge: Multilingual Reasoning Without Multilingual Supervision
candidates.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
candidates.summary: LangBridge considerably enhances the performance of language models on low-resource languages across mathematical reasoning, code completion, logical reasoning, and commonsense reasoning.

candidates.title: Explicitly Encoding Structural Symmetry is Key to Length Generalization in Arithmetic Tasks
candidates.venue: arXiv.org
candidates.summary: It is proved that explicit incorporation of structure via positional encodings is necessary for out-of-distribution generalization, and pinpoint other challenges inherent to length generalization beyond capturing symmetries, in particular complexity of the underlying task.

candidates.title: WinoWhat: A Parallel Corpus of Paraphrased WinoGrande Sentences with Common Sense Categorization
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 29th Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
candidates.summary: This study evaluates generative models of different sizes on the popular WinoGrande benchmark, and releases WinoWhat, a new corpus, in which each instance of the WinoGrande validation set is paraphrased.

candidates.title: AgentCoMa: A Compositional Benchmark Mixing Commonsense and Mathematical Reasoning in Real-World Scenarios
candidates.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
candidates.summary: This work introduces an Agentic Commonsense and Math benchmark (AgentCoMa), where each compositional task requires a commonsense reasoning step and a math reasoning step, and finds that LLMs can usually solve both steps in isolation, yet their accuracy drops by nearly 30% on average when the two are combined.

candidates.title: Self-Organizing Group Network for learning primary mathematics from natural language
candidates.venue: Knowledge-Based Systems

candidates.title: GenBERTplus : A New Approach to Numeracy in Natural Language Processing
candidates.venue: Conference Information and Communication Technology
